questions.prompt: State the size of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&4&0\\-2&5&7\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer:
Count rows first and columns second. The matrix has \(2\) rows and \(3\) columns, so its size is
\[
2\times3.
\]

questions.prompt: For \(B=\begin{pmatrix}6&-1\\0&3\\8&2\end{pmatrix}\), identify \(b_{31}\).
questions.answer:
The notation \(b_{ij}\) means row \(i\), column \(j\). Thus \(b_{31}\) is in row \(3\), column \(1\). In the matrix, row \(3\) is \((8,2)\), so
\[
b_{31}=8.
\]

questions.prompt: Is \(\begin{pmatrix}2\\-5\\1\end{pmatrix}\) a row vector or a column vector? Give its size.
questions.answer:
The entries are stacked vertically, so there is one column. There are \(3\) rows and \(1\) column, hence the size is
\[
3\times1.
\]
It is a column vector.

questions.prompt: Write the set notation for all real \(4\times2\) matrices.
questions.answer:
The set of real \(m\times n\) matrices is written \(\operatorname{Mat}_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)\). With \(m=4\) and \(n=2\), the required set is
\[
\operatorname{Mat}_{4\times2}(\mathbb R).
\]

questions.prompt: For \(C=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&-4\\1&9&2\\7&6&5\end{pmatrix}\), find \(c_{12}\) and \(c_{23}\).
questions.answer:
Use row first, column second. The entry \(c_{12}\) is in row \(1\), column \(2\), so
\[
c_{12}=0.
\]
The entry \(c_{23}\) is in row \(2\), column \(3\), so
\[
c_{23}=2.
\]

questions.prompt: A matrix has entries \(a_{ij}=i+j\) for \(1\le i\le2\), \(1\le j\le3\). Write the matrix.
questions.answer:
Compute each entry by row and column. Row \(1\):
\[
a_{11}=2,\quad a_{12}=3,\quad a_{13}=4.
\]
Row \(2\):
\[
a_{21}=3,\quad a_{22}=4,\quad a_{23}=5.
\]
Therefore
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&3&4\\3&4&5\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: Decide whether \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\3&4&5\\6&7&8\end{pmatrix}\) is square, and state the value of \(n\) if its size is \(n\times n\).
questions.answer:
The matrix has \(3\) rows and \(3\) columns. Since the row count equals the column count, it is square. Its size is
\[
3\times3,
\]
so \(n=3\).

questions.prompt: A learner says a \(2\times5\) matrix has \(5\) rows and \(2\) columns. Correct the statement.
questions.answer: Matrix size is always written as rows by columns. Therefore a \(2\times5\) matrix has \(2\) rows and \(5\) columns, not \(5\) rows and \(2\) columns.

questions.prompt: Let \(A\in\operatorname{Mat}_{2\times4}(\mathbb R)\). How many entries does \(A\) have, and what are the possible row and column indices?
questions.answer:
A \(2\times4\) matrix has \(2\) rows and \(4\) columns, so the number of entries is
\[
2\cdot4=8.
\]
The row index can be \(i=1\) or \(i=2\). The column index can be \(j=1,2,3,4\). Thus entries have labels \(a_{ij}\) with \(1\le i\le2\) and \(1\le j\le4\).

questions.prompt: Construct a \(2\times3\) matrix \(A\) with \(a_{ij}=2i-j\).
questions.answer:
Compute row by row. For \(i=1\):
\[
a_{11}=1,\quad a_{12}=0,\quad a_{13}=-1.
\]
For \(i=2\):
\[
a_{21}=3,\quad a_{22}=2,\quad a_{23}=1.
\]
So
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\3&2&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

questions.prompt: Explain why a column vector with \(5\) entries belongs to \(\operatorname{Mat}_{5\times1}(\mathbb R)\), not \(\operatorname{Mat}_{1\times5}(\mathbb R)\).
questions.answer:
A column vector stacks entries vertically. Five vertical entries mean \(5\) rows. Since it is a column vector, it has exactly \(1\) column. Matrix size is rows by columns, so its size is
\[
5\times1.
\]
A \(1\times5\) matrix would have one row and five columns, which is a row vector instead.

questions.prompt: Given \(D=\begin{pmatrix}d_{11}&d_{12}\\d_{21}&d_{22}\\d_{31}&d_{32}\end{pmatrix}\), explain which symbol names the entry in the bottom-right position.
questions.answer:
The bottom row is row \(3\), and the right column is column \(2\). Entry notation uses row index first and column index second. Therefore the bottom-right entry is
\[
d_{32}.
\]

questions.prompt: A data table stores displacement components \((x,y,z)\) for \(4\) particles, with one particle per row and one component per column. What matrix size represents the table, and what does entry \(a_{23}\) mean?
questions.answer:
There are \(4\) particles, so there are \(4\) rows. There are three components \((x,y,z)\), so there are \(3\) columns. The matrix size is
\[
4\times3.
\]
The entry \(a_{23}\) is row \(2\), column \(3\), so it is the third component, \(z\), of the second particle.

questions.prompt: A matrix \(A\) has \(12\) entries and \(3\) rows. If it is not a row vector, what is its size?
questions.answer:
The number of entries equals rows times columns. If there are \(12\) entries and \(3\) rows, then
\[
3\cdot n=12.
\]
So \(n=4\). The matrix has \(3\) rows and \(4\) columns, hence its size is
\[
3\times4.
\]
It is not a row vector because a row vector would have one row.

questions.prompt: Find all possible sizes of a real matrix with \(6\) entries that is not square. Use positive row and column counts.
questions.answer:
If the matrix has \(m\) rows and \(n\) columns, then
\[
mn=6.
\]
The positive factor pairs are \((1,6)\), \((2,3)\), \((3,2)\), and \((6,1)\). None of these has equal row and column counts, so none is square. The possible sizes are
\[
1\times6,\quad 2\times3,\quad 3\times2,\quad 6\times1.
\]

questions.prompt: For an \(m\times n\) matrix \(A\), the entry \(a_{47}\) is defined but \(a_{74}\) is not. Give one possible pair \((m,n)\) and explain the restrictions.
questions.answer:
For \(a_{47}\) to be defined, the matrix must have at least \(4\) rows and at least \(7\) columns, so \(m\ge4\) and \(n\ge7\). For \(a_{74}\) not to be defined, row \(7\) must not exist or column \(4\) must not exist. Since \(n\ge7\), column \(4\) exists, so row \(7\) must not exist. Thus \(m<7\). One possible choice is
\[
(m,n)=(4,7).
\]

questions.prompt: A matrix \(A\in\operatorname{Mat}_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)\) is both a row vector and a column vector. Determine \(m\) and \(n\).
questions.answer:
A row vector has one row, so \(m=1\). A column vector has one column, so \(n=1\). If both descriptions are true, the matrix has size
\[
1\times1.
\]
Therefore \(m=1\) and \(n=1\).

questions.prompt: Diagnose the error: for \(A=\begin{pmatrix}5&6&7\\8&9&10\end{pmatrix}\), a learner says \(a_{23}=6\).
questions.answer:
The notation \(a_{23}\) means row \(2\), column \(3\), not row \(3\), column \(2\), and not the second entry in row \(1\). Row \(2\) is
\[
(8,9,10).
\]
The third entry of that row is \(10\). Therefore
\[
a_{23}=10,
\]
and the learner likely reversed or misread the indexing order.

questions.prompt: Prove that an \(m\times n\) matrix is square exactly when \(m=n\).
questions.answer: By definition, an \(m\times n\) matrix has \(m\) rows and \(n\) columns. A square matrix is defined as a matrix whose number of rows equals its number of columns. Therefore, if the matrix is square, its row count and column count are equal, so \(m=n\). Conversely, if \(m=n\), the matrix has the same number of rows and columns, so it is square. Hence an \(m\times n\) matrix is square exactly when \(m=n\).

questions.prompt: A physics list records \(n\) time samples of three quantities \(s\), \(v\), and \(a\). One convention stores samples as rows; another stores quantities as rows. Compare the two matrix sizes and explain why the same data can have different notation.
questions.answer:
If each time sample is a row, then there are \(n\) rows and \(3\) columns, one for each of \(s\), \(v\), and \(a\). The size is
\[
n\times3.
\]
If each quantity is a row, then there are \(3\) rows and \(n\) columns, one for each time sample. The size is
\[
3\times n.
\]
The numerical data can be the same measurements, but the indexing convention changes which feature is represented by rows and which is represented by columns. Clear notation is needed before interpreting entries such as \(a_{ij}\).
